proof.text:
Fix $m\ge n$, put $A=A_m$, $B=A_n$, and write $T_W=-\otimes^L_{A_W}B_W$ and $U_W$ for restriction, also on the point module categories. All sites are taken in the module universe. Use the fixed compactification in the statement throughout. Let $d:C_m\otimes_A^LB\xrightarrow{\sim}C_n$ be its coefficient comparison followed by point sections, and let $\alpha_r:C\otimes_R^LA_r\xrightarrow{\sim}C_r$ be the comparisons assumed in the statement. Their specified successive-reduction normalization gives
$$d\circ(\alpha_m\otimes_A^LB)=\alpha_n.$$
Here and below the canonical scalar tensor reassociations are understood. We use precisely these supplied comparisons, not an independently chosen isomorphism between the endpoints. The finite input $K_r$ is bounded constructible and has finite Tor amplitude by hypothesis; the same properties of $\omega_r$ are included in the finite dualizing result and the assumed finite Tor amplitude of $\omega_r$. Thus coefficient comparisons at $K_m$ and $\omega_m$ are isomorphisms.

proof.text:
Use the evaluation-normalized scalar-Hom isomorphism of [lem-sfb-dc-hom-scalar-adjunction] for $R_X\to(A_r)_X$ and, on the one-object module site, for $R\to A_r$. It is natural in both arguments and commutes with coefficient ring maps; there is no flatness assumption on $A\to B$. In particular postcomposition by $\operatorname{Res}_m\tau_{m,n}$ on $H_m$ is the scalar-adjoint version of
$$f_m\longmapsto f_n=u_{m,n}\circ T_X(f_m).$$
To spell out its meaning, take an arbitrary $P\in D(R)$ and $h:P\to H_m$. Put $P_r=P\otimes_R^LA_r$, and let $(P_r)_X$ denote its constant complex on $X$. The global-sections adjunction and tensor-Hom transposition identify $h$ with an evaluation map
$$f_m:(P_m)_X\otimes_A^LK_m\longrightarrow\omega_m.$$
The corresponding map for the left transition applied to $h$ is the displayed $f_n$, with $T_X((P_m)_X\otimes_A^LK_m)\cong(P_n)_X\otimes_B^LK_n$. The formula follows also directly from the scalar-adjunction unit $x\mapsto x\otimes1$: the adjunct of $\tau_{m,n}f_m$ sends $x\otimes b$ to $b\tau_{m,n}f_m(x)$, which is $u_{m,n}T_X(f_m)$.

proof.text:
The finite dualizing node states, with its indices renamed $A=A_m$, $B=A_n$,
$$\varepsilon_n\circ F_n(u_{m,n})=(T_s\varepsilon_m)\circ c_{m,n,\omega_m}^{-1}.$$
Its last clause identifies this counit-defined map with its finite pro-etale realization, so this is the identity for the functors in this item. This already proves the trace assertion, including its specified normalization. Equivalently, without an inverse on the right,
$$\varepsilon_n F_n(u_{m,n})c_{m,n,\omega_m}=T_s\varepsilon_m.$$
We will use this last equality when composing the evaluation pairings. Restriction of compact support along $A\to B$ is the canonical one for the same compactification, by [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars].

proof.text: The coefficient square for the proper factor is a square of ringed topoi: its two vertical arrows are $p$ at $A$ and $B$, and its horizontal arrows are the identity underlying topos with structural ring map $A_W\to B_W$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] to this square. Its pullbacks along the horizontal arrows are exactly $T_W$. Its exchange is the canonical proper coefficient map, with this normalization by [lem-sp-direct-image-change-ring-transpose]. Hence the proper projection map commutes with coefficient change for every input and every tensor parameter, without requiring any exchange to be invertible. The same generic ringed-topos statement applies to the sections morphism from $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ to the one-object coefficient site. Sections are the derived direct image for this morphism, and are computed termwise here by [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. These applications are legitimate for arbitrary $P_m$, not only constructible parameters.

proof.text: For the open factor use [lem-cbc-extension-zero-projection-formula]. With coefficient parameter $B_{\overline X}$ it gives the canonical comparison $T_{\overline X}j_!M\cong j_!T_XM$, before forgetting the $B$ action: on total-tensor representatives it is the balanced map $(j_!x)\otimes b\mapsto j_!(x\otimes b)$. To justify these representatives, choose a K-flat flat-term resolution $Q\to M$. The open tensor formula and exactness of $j_!$ and $j^*$ show $j_!Q$ is K-flat, since tensoring it with an acyclic complex is $j_!$ of $Q$ tensored with an acyclic restriction. For two tensor factors, scalar change of the open projection map and the open projection after scalar change restrict to the identical balanced tensor map on $X$; the $j_!\dashv j^*$ bijection makes them equal on $\overline X$. Tensor reassociation respects the $B$ action by $b(x\otimes y)=(bx)\otimes y$. Therefore, substituting this open identity and the proper identity of step 4 into the defining composite $\operatorname{PF}^c=Rp_*(\gamma_j)\pi_p$ proves coefficient compatibility of the compact-support projection map. This is just pasting those two identities in the fixed compactification; no compactification-independence theorem or inverse projection map is needed.

Transpose step 8 under tensor-Hom adjunction in $D(R)$. By steps 2 and 6 its two maps $P\to J_n$ are respectively
$$J(q)\,\widetilde\gamma_mh\quad\text{and}\quad\widetilde\gamma_n H(\operatorname{Res}_m\tau_{m,n})h.$$

proof.text: For a morphism $z:K\to K'$ between objects satisfying the hypotheses, the maps on $H_r$ are precomposition by $z$ (or $z_r$ after scalar adjunction), and the maps on $J_r$ are precomposition by $C(z):C\to C'$. The current [lem-coef-finite-mapping-adjunction] states that $\gamma_{r,M}$ is a canonical natural isomorphism for every finite constructible finite-Tor $M$, so it applies to both $K_r$ and $K'_r$ and is natural in $z_r$. The scalar-Hom comparison and $\alpha_r$ are natural as well. Explicitly, the evaluation relation is $f'_r(1\otimes z_r)$; inserting it in step 6 replaces compact support by $F_r(z_r)$, hence replaces the pairing by precomposition with $1\otimes C_r(z_r)$. It follows after transposition that $J_r(C(z))\widetilde\gamma_{r,K'}=\widetilde\gamma_{r,K}H_r(z)$. Precomposition by $z$ commutes with postcomposition by $\tau_{m,n}$, and precomposition by $C(z)$ commutes with postcomposition by $q$. Thus the proved squares are contravariantly natural in $K$. When $m=n$ the coefficient units and $u_{m,m}=1$ give the identity square; when $K=0$ or $X$ is empty all pairings have zero source. These cases require no additional hypothesis.

title: Finite-level adjunction transition compatibility
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Fix a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $a:X\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ be separated and of finite type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use ordinary module sheaves on the small pro-etale sites, with completed coefficient sheaf $R_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$ for $W=X,s$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Write $F_n=Ra_{!,n}$ for compact support using one fixed compactification $a=pj$ [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], $G_n=Ra_n^!$ for the finite constructible comparison-class exceptional functor [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and $\omega_n=G_n(A_n)_s$. Let $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], let $K_n=K\otimes^L_{R_X}(A_n)_X$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction], and suppose its reductions have Tor amplitude in one finite interval $[a_0,b_0]$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Put $C_n=\Gamma(s,F_nK_n)$ and $C=\Gamma(s,Ra_!K)$, with coefficient-point sections [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Suppose also that $\omega_n$ has finite Tor amplitude for every $n$. Let $u_{m,n}:\omega_m\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_n$ be the counit-defined map of [lem-coef-finite-dualizing], with adjunct $\tau_{m,n}:\omega_m\to\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}\omega_n$. Let $c_{m,n}: (F_mK_m)\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}F_nK_n$ and $C\otimes_R^LA_n\xrightarrow{\sim}C_n$ be the canonical compact-support and point-section comparisons [lem-coef-integral-compact-support] [lem-pod-point-sections-derived-reduction]. Set
$$H_n=\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_{R_X}(K,\operatorname{Res}_n\omega_n),\qquad J_n=\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_R(C,A_n)$$
using global mapping complexes [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Identify $H_n$ with $\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_{X,A_n}(K_n,\omega_n)$ by derived tensor-restriction adjunction. Compose $\gamma_{n,K_n}$ of [lem-coef-finite-mapping-adjunction] with the analogous scalar-adjunction identification on $C$ to obtain $\widetilde\gamma_n:H_n\xrightarrow{\sim}J_n$. For every $m\ge n$, the square whose horizontal maps are $\widetilde\gamma_m,\widetilde\gamma_n$, whose left vertical map is induced by $\operatorname{Res}_m\tau_{m,n}$ and whose right vertical map is induced by $A_m\twoheadrightarrow A_n$, commutes in $D(R)$. These squares are contravariantly natural in $K$. The finite traces themselves obey
$$\varepsilon_n\circ F_n(u_{m,n})=(\varepsilon_m\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n)\circ c_{m,n,\omega_m}^{-1},$$
with $c_{m,n,\omega_m}$ the finite compact-support coefficient comparison [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change].
